channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: South Korean Cabinet Revamp Fails to Stem Slide in Lee Support
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung’s approval rating slid to a fresh record low, a sign that his surprise cabinet reshuffle failed to immediately shore up public sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Soobin Kim

item.title: Japan Needs to Stand Firm Against US Pressure, Lawmaker Says
item.description: Japan needs to stand firm against US pressure as its close security ally challenges international norms and laws under President Donald Trump’s “America First” agenda, according to a veteran Japanese lawmaker.
item.dc:creator: Alastair Gale and Sakura Murakami

item.title: Greer Says He’s ‘Optimistic’ About Relations With China Before Trump-Xi Summit
item.description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer struck a positive tone on relations with China weeks before a summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, despite underlying disagreements between the two nations.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Chua

item.title: Argentina’s Milei Revives Bitter Falklands Dispute With UK
item.description: Argentina’s Javier Milei is reviving his country’s bitter clash with the UK over the Falkland Islands, targeting a new oil project in the disputed area in strident terms as the popularity of his presidency sinks.
item.dc:creator: Manuela Tobias and Jonathan Gilbert

item.title: South Korea Paving Way to Send Troops to Hormuz, Reports Say
item.description: South Korea has begun preparations for a possible deployment of a naval support ship and troops to the Strait of Hormuz, local media reports said, as President Donald Trump ramped up pressure on the US ally over its lack of support for the war with Iran.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Trump Attacks Missouri’s High Court Over Redistricting Decision
item.description: President Donald Trump assailed a decision by the Missouri Supreme Court that cast aside a congressional map engineered by state Republicans, likely allowing Democrats to retain a House seat in November’s midterm elections they would’ve almost certainly otherwise lost.
item.dc:creator: John Harney

item.title: JD Vance on Iran: ‘I Wouldn’t Call It a War'
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Jim McGovern (D-MA), the top Democrat on the House Rules Committee, says his conversations with constituents are dominated by concerns around the cost of living, arguing voters want Congress focused on lowering prices ahead of the midterm elections. Vladyslav Vlasiuk, Presidential Commissioner for Sanctions Policy of Ukraine, says Congress should pass a sweeping Russia sanctions bill "now," arguing additional economic pressure is needed to constrain Moscow's ability to fund the war. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Powerful Brazil Judge Faces Reckoning Over Ties to $10 Billion Bank Scandal
item.description: For the past seven years, no member of Brazil’s Supreme Court has exercised its vast powers as forcefully as Alexandre de Moraes.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho and Martha Beck

item.title: Trump Names Adam Telle Acting Army Secretary After Driscoll Exit
item.description: President Donald Trump named Adam Telle as acting secretary of the US Army, elevating the current assistant secretary overseeing civil works following the resignation of Army Secretary Dan Driscoll.
item.dc:creator: Jen Judson and Derek Wallbank

item.title: Alger EVP: Still Massive Opportunity for AI
item.description: Ankur Crawford, Executive Vice President and Portfolio Manager at Alger, says political backlash around AI infrastructure could become a future constraint on data center and chip buildout, though it has not yet materially slowed projects. She argues that much of the opposition is driven by misinformation and that the key risk for investors is confusion, which can create volatility. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. McGovern: Cuba Becoming a "Slow-Moving Gaza"
item.description: Rep. Jim McGovern (D-MA), the top Democrat on the House Rules Committee, says his conversations with constituents are dominated by concerns around the cost of living, arguing voters want Congress focused on lowering prices ahead of the midterm elections. Rep. McGovern, a longtime advocate for normalizing relations with Cuba, says US efforts to economically isolate the country are contributing to severe energy shortages and calls the approach a policy that "constitutes a human rights violation." He also criticizes Trump's attacks on mail-in voting, as the Justice Department asks the Supreme Court to weigh in on a dispute over mail ballots. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Work on Trump’s Memorial Arch to Start Over Next Two Weeks
item.description: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said Thursday construction work would begin on President Donald Trump’s proposed memorial arch, as the administration proceeds with a project that has drawn backlash over its size and location.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan

item.title: Ukraine's Vlasiuk Says Russia Sanctions Bill Will Send 'Strong Signal'
item.description: Ukraine Sanctions Policy Commissioner Vladyslav Vlasiuk says Congress should pass a sweeping Russia sanctions bill "now," arguing additional economic pressure is needed to constrain Moscow's ability to fund the war. He speaks on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: FCC Tells Judge Trump Clash With ABC Isn’t About Free Speech
item.description: The US Federal Communications Commission asked a judge to toss out ABC’s lawsuit accusing the regulator of waging an unconstitutional “retaliatory campaign” against the network as punishment for programming criticized by the Trump administration.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson

item.title: Nvidia to Buy Hugging Face for $13B | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 9/3/2026
item.description: Nvidia agreed to acquire artificial intelligence startup Hugging Face in a transaction valued at about $13 billion, adding a popular software platform to the chip giant’s AI empire. The price includes an equity-based retention program of as much as $1 billion for Hugging Face employees who join Nvidia, according to a statement Thursday. Bloomberg News AI reporter Rachel Metz discussed the acquisition and Bloomberg Tech Host Ed Ludlow discussed his interview with Hugging Face Co-Founder Thomas Wolf. Plus, Jason Tyler, President of Northern Trust Wealth Management talked about the private credit market. Finally, Randall Williams, Bloomberg News Senior Sports Reporter discussed the NBA's suspension of Steve Ballmer. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Tariff Regime Prompts Supply Chain Concerns Over Kosher Food
item.description: A tariff investigation in President Donald Trump’s administration has spurred an unlikely critic: one of the largest Orthodox Jewish groups in the US.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Diaz

item.title: Farage’s Bid to Reset Reform UK Fortunes Hit By Undercover Sting
item.description: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage’s hopes of using a keynote speech at his party’s annual convention to arrest a slide in opinion polls were upended after two of his closest allies were covertly filmed discussing avoiding electoral law to secure foreign donations.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: September Jobs Report to Give Economic Reality Check Before Midterms
item.description: It could help drive a decision on interest rates, a potential pitfall for the GOP.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: Supreme Court Asked to Allow Mail Ballot Curbs for Midterms
item.description: The Trump administration asked the US Supreme Court to let the Postal Service enforce new rules for mail-in ballots ahead of the November midterm elections, a move that some states have warned would wreak havoc as they prepare to send ballots to voters in the coming days.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: Lula-Backed Bill to Trim Workweek Delayed in Fresh Setback
item.description: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s flagship legislative proposal to reduce Brazilians’ workweek without a change in pay was delayed in the Senate Thursday, dealing the incumbent a setback as he looks to regain momentum ahead of a tight October election.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho
